findings.text: blocking: The Solov'ev known state never converges or recovers: 24 passes, flux error 2.889 of the span against the 1e-6 band, terminal residual 0.9347 against 1e-8, last update 0.2849 of the span, and the record itself reads 'bands not met'. Done-when clause (1) requires all three Section 1 known states to converge and recover inside the bands, and the four relaxation arms (html:41-48, at 0.5, 0.25 and 0.10) each end without a contraction. Either land an estimator that recovers this state or obtain a plan decision that holds the section open.

blocking: The terminal-state contour group (TriContourSet_2, stroke #3366cc) holds 12 paths whose d attribute is empty, so the panel draws the grey reference map only, while the caption at html:19 claims 'narrow blue contours of the terminal state the fit laid down'. The binding plotting rule says a panel that shows a solved field draws both sets and that a figure breaking the rule is regenerated rather than captioned around; the stored-case painter already handles the disjoint-level case by drawing nova on its own levels and labelling them (tests/test_magnetics_fit_efit_comparison.py:1479-1505), and the known-state painter has no such branch (tests/test_equilibrium_magnetics_fit.py:1750-1797).

non-blocking: The published record was produced by six separate scheduler jobs (1327572 for the six rows, 1327685/1327710/1327819/1327990 for the relaxation arms, 1327987 for the re-rendered Solov'ev panel), and the text states so: 'The runs are separate jobs, not one measurement.' Done-when clause (3) and the repository's one-measurement-one-job rule require one batch job that runs the cases in sequence inside its allocation; the numbers agree where compared, so this is a provenance defect in the evidence rather than a wrong measurement, but the receipt does not have the shape the section names.

non-blocking: The conductor-response validation, per-column naming, uniqueness check and read-only freeze at nova/equilibrium/flux_iteration.py:164-183 duplicate the block at nova/equilibrium/magnetics_fit.py:227-243, differing only in where the current vector comes from. The node already extracted the coefficient basis into that module as the shared owner (magnetics_fit.py:78-159), so that idiom is established and this residual block could share it; duplicating it lets the two fitters drift in what they accept.

non-blocking: update is computed from the full delta at line 406, before line 415 lays down flux + relaxation * delta, so IterationPass.flux_update is unrelaxed although the docstring at :65-66 calls it 'the largest flux change of the update that pass applies'. Every damping arm in the record therefore overstates its 'last update / span' by 1/relaxation (the 0.10 arm reports 0.07204 for an applied 0.0072), and that is the quantity done-when (2) asks a reader to lay the failure beside the misfit with.
